Incorporating the Federal Reserve’s Financial Stability Report lens, the policy tone remains moderately hawkish. The statement’s “ongoing increases” and continued QT point to tighter financial conditions, and the FSR highlights channels that amplify restrictiveness beyond the policy rate: thinner Treasury market liquidity and elevated rate/term-premium sensitivity, nonbank funding risks (e.g., MMFs, leveraged funds), and vulnerabilities in interest-rate–sensitive sectors (housing/CRE). These reinforce the hawkish tilt. That said, the Committee’s emphasis on cumulative tightening and policy lags is consistent with the FSR’s risk-management caution, tempering the degree of hawkishness versus late-2022. Net effect: slightly more negative than neutral, modestly more restrictive than a rate-only read.
